contraception.name: Contraception
contraception.scope: Combined oral contraceptives, progestin-only pills, implant, intrauterine devices, tubal sterilization
contraception.core: Choose contraception through shared decisions about efficacy, bleeding, reversibility, adherence, and estrogen-related vascular risk.

rows.label: Who
items: Anyone seeking pregnancy prevention; adolescents and nulliparous patients can use IUDs or implants
Healthy patient: blood pressure suffices; **no pelvic exam** needed before oral contraceptives

rows.label: Schedule
items: Pills daily; depot medroxyprogesterone every 3 months; implants/IUDs last years (product-dependent)
★ Emergency contraception ≤**5 days**: copper IUD/ulipristal; levonorgestrel ≤72 h, no medical contraindications
Progestin-only pills: daily timing crucial; norethindrone less forgiving than drospirenone

rows.label: Special groups
items: Breastfeeding (estrogen lowers milk volume, protein) or estrogen contraindication → progestin-only or copper IUD
Current breast cancer → copper IUD; avoid hormonal methods
Prior VTE, poor adherence → **IUD/implant** (depot raises VTE risk); older exams: depot, avoid IUD after STI

rows.label: Choice
items: Combined pills: suppress ovulation, improve acne/cramps, reduce endometrial/ovarian cancer risk
★ **LARC** minimizes adherence failures; condoms add STI protection
Tubal sterilization: permanent; counsel regret, alternatives, surgical risk, ectopic risk after failure

rows.label: Contraindications
items: ★ Estrogen: **migraine with aura, prior VTE/thrombophilia**, hypertension (stop pill), early postpartum
Smoking age ≥35: combined methods usually avoid; ≥15 cigarettes/day → absolute contraindication
IUD: pregnancy, cervicitis/PID, distorted cavity (non-distorting fibroid OK); copper: also Wilson disease

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Same-day STI screening need not delay insertion without cervicitis; prior PID alone permits IUD
Sterilization: voluntary informed consent; no required partner approval, parity, or marital status
After ulipristal, wait 5 days before progestin; backup contraception needed after hormonal restart

table.title: Long-acting choices
rows: Treats heavy menses; atrophy → expected benign amenorrhea

early-pregnancy-loss.name: Early pregnancy loss
early-pregnancy-loss.scope: Threatened abortion, inevitable abortion, incomplete abortion, complete abortion, missed abortion, anembryonic pregnancy
early-pregnancy-loss.core: First-trimester bleeding requires pregnancy location and viability assessment before labeling miscarriage or choosing expectant, medical, or surgical management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Embryonic aneuploidy most common; maternal age, prior losses, uterine anomalies, antiphospholipid syndrome

rows.label: Clues
items: Cramping, vaginal bleeding, passage of tissue; symptoms may be absent with retained nonviable pregnancy
★ Hypotension, syncope, peritoneal signs → **hemorrhage or ruptured ectopic**
Fever, uterine tenderness, foul discharge → septic abortion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Embryonic/fetal demise or failed embryonic development → decidual separation and variable cervical dilation
Corpus luteum progesterone sustains pregnancy until ~10 weeks; removal earlier → **progesterone supplementation**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Transvaginal ultrasound** plus quantitative β-hCG; CBC, blood type, pelvic examination
Definitive nonviability: CRL ≥7 mm without heartbeat or mean sac diameter ≥25 mm without embryo
Absent embryo/heartbeat on repeat: ≥11 days after yolk sac, ≥14 days after sac-only → nonviable
No intrauterine pregnancy → serial hCG/ultrasound; tissue passage alone cannot exclude ectopic

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable, infected, or uncontrolled hemorrhage → **urgent uterine aspiration**; sepsis → IV broad-spectrum antibiotics
Confirmed stable loss → patient choice: observation, mifepristone followed by misoprostol, or aspiration
Threatened loss → expectant follow-up; bed rest does not prevent miscarriage
Stable, unlocated pregnancy, falling hCG → serial hCG until negative; no methotrexate
★ Rh-negative loss **≥12 weeks → RhIg**; ACOG omits routine testing earlier; older exam questions may expect Rh typing

rows.label: Complications
items: Retained products, infection, hemorrhage; intrauterine adhesions after instrumentation; grief/depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking/alcohol avoidance, optimize diabetes; most isolated chromosomal losses unpreventable
Recurrent clinical losses → assess uterine anatomy, antiphospholipid antibodies and selected genetic causes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: extrauterine implantation, adnexal mass/free fluid
Gestational trophoblastic disease: very high hCG, abnormal cystic intrauterine tissue
Subchorionic hematoma: bleeding without cramping; viable intrauterine pregnancy, perichorionic collection
Normal early pregnancy: spotting, 5-week sac, hCG ~1,000, simple corpus luteum cyst; embryo not yet expected

ectopic-pregnancy.name: Ectopic pregnancy
ectopic-pregnancy.scope: Diagnosis (beta-hCG, transvaginal ultrasound, discriminatory zone), unruptured ectopic pregnancy, medical management (methotrexate), ruptured ectopic pregnancy, surgical management
ectopic-pregnancy.core: Pregnancy implanted outside the endometrial cavity, usually tubal; early pregnancy with pelvic pain or bleeding requires localization and rupture assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior ectopic, PID/tubal damage, tubal surgery, infertility treatment, smoking
IUDs prevent pregnancy overall; pregnancy despite IUD has higher ectopic proportion; many cases lack risks

rows.label: Clues
items: Amenorrhea, unilateral pelvic pain, spotting; cervical motion/adnexal tenderness nonspecific
★ **Syncope, shoulder-tip pain, peritoneal signs, hypotension** → hemoperitoneum/rupture
Heterotopic pregnancy possible despite visualized intrauterine pregnancy, particularly after assisted reproduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired tubal transport → extrauterine trophoblastic implantation, invasion, hemorrhage
Methotrexate inhibits folate-dependent DNA synthesis in proliferating trophoblast

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test → quantitative beta-hCG + transvaginal ultrasound**; ultrasound regardless of hCG when symptomatic
Extrauterine yolk sac/embryo diagnostic; adnexal mass/free fluid supportive; empty uterus alone insufficient
★ Stable pregnancy of unknown location → **repeat hCG in 48 hours**, serial ultrasound until resolved/localized
Subnormal 48-hour hCG rise + empty uterus + pain → suspect **ectopic**; rapid fall favors miscarriage
Discriminatory threshold up to 3,500 mIU/mL protects viable IUP; abnormal rise/fall cannot establish location

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable/rupture concern → **IV access, blood resuscitation, urgent laparotomy**; do not await serial hCG
Confirmed unruptured, stable, reliable follow-up, hCG <5,000, mass <3.5 cm, no fetal heartbeat → consider **methotrexate**
Avoid methotrexate: viable IUP, breastfeeding, hepatic/renal disease, cytopenias, immunodeficiency, unreliable follow-up
Postmethotrexate hCG days 4/7: fall ≥15% → weekly until negative; inadequate fall → reassess/re-dose/surgery

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhagic shock, death, tubal loss, recurrence, impaired fertility
Methotrexate: mucositis, hepatotoxicity, marrow suppression; rupture remains possible despite falling hCG

rows.label: Prevention
items: Treat/prevent STIs, smoking cessation; prior ectopic → early ultrasound in subsequent pregnancy
Methotrexate counseling: avoid alcohol, folate supplements, intercourse until resolution; avoid conception for 3 months
Unsensitized Rh-negative ectopic → Rh(D) immune globulin; provide return precautions for escalating pain/dizziness

rows.label: Mimics
items: Miscarriage: intrauterine pregnancy loss; passage of decidual tissue alone does not prove IUP
Hemorrhagic corpus luteum: ovarian source, may coexist with normal pregnancy
Ovarian torsion: abrupt severe unilateral pain, enlarged ovary

table.title: Alternative definitive branches
rows: Stable, minimal symptoms, low declining hCG
Selected expectant management with reliable surveillance
Heartbeat, high hCG, severe pain, or contraindication

ectopic-pregnancy.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG ectopic pregnancy](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/ectopic-pregnancy), [NICE tubal ectopic management](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/NG126/chapter/management-of-tubal-ectopic-pregnancy); conservative discriminatory threshold established ACOG teaching.

gestational-diabetes-mellitus.name: Gestational diabetes mellitus
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Screening (50g oral glucose challenge at 24-28 weeks), diagnostic 3-hour 100g test, glycemic targets, nutritional therapy, insulin, fetal and neonatal complications (macrosomia, hypoglycemia, RDS, polycythemia)
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.core: Pregnancy-induced insulin resistance unmasks hyperglycemia, increasing fetal insulin secretion and growth; screen routinely at 24–28 weeks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, prior GDM/macrosomia, family history of type 2 diabetes, PCOS
High-risk patients need early assessment for previously unrecognized overt diabetes

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; excessive fetal growth or polyhydramnios may prompt evaluation
Early marked hyperglycemia suggests preexisting diabetes rather than typical later-onset GDM

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental hormones increase maternal insulin requirements; inadequate beta-cell compensation causes dysglycemia
Maternal glucose crosses placenta; insulin does not; fetal hyperinsulinemia persists briefly after birth
Fetal hyperinsulinemia → macrosomia; antagonizes cortisol → less surfactant, **RDS**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Two-step screen: **nonfasting 50 g challenge**, 1-hour threshold 130–140 mg/dL by local protocol
Positive challenge → fasting 100 g, 3-hour OGTT; **≥2 abnormal values** diagnose GDM
Alternative one-step 75 g OGTT: fasting ≥92, 1-hour ≥180, or 2-hour ≥153 mg/dL
HbA1c alone does not replace pregnancy glucose testing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First: **individualized nutrition, activity, home glucose monitoring**; avoid severe carbohydrate restriction
★ Targets: fasting **<95**, 1-hour <140, or 2-hour <120 mg/dL
Above targets despite lifestyle → **insulin preferred**; metformin crosses placenta, counsel if used
Medication need or poor control → fetal surveillance; delivery timing depends on control and obstetric findings
Suspected fetal weight ≥4,500 g with diabetes → discuss planned cesarean

rows.label: Complications
items: Maternal: preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, future type 2 diabetes
Fetal: macrosomia, shoulder dystocia, birth trauma; poor control increases stillbirth risk
Neonate: **hypoglycemia**, RDS, polycythemia, jaundice; congenital anomalies mainly reflect pregestational diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Postpartum **75 g OGTT at 4–12 weeks**; lifelong diabetes testing every 1–3 years
Breastfeeding, weight management, activity; most GDM insulin needs resolve after placental delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pregestational diabetes: overt diagnostic-range hyperglycemia early in pregnancy
Physiologic glycosuria: lower renal threshold without diagnostic blood glucose abnormalities

gestational-trophoblastic-disease.name: Gestational trophoblastic disease
gestational-trophoblastic-disease.scope: Complete hydatidiform mole, partial hydatidiform mole, choriocarcinoma, suction curettage, serial beta-hCG surveillance, contraception
gestational-trophoblastic-disease.core: Abnormal trophoblastic proliferation causes excessive hCG, bleeding, and vesicular placental tissue; persistent hCG after evacuation suggests gestational trophoblastic neoplasia.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior molar pregnancy, extremes of reproductive age; choriocarcinoma can follow any pregnancy

rows.label: Clues
items: Vaginal bleeding, hyperemesis, uterus larger than dates, bilateral theca lutein cysts
★ **Preeclampsia before 20 weeks** or gestational thyrotoxicosis → suspect mole
Postpregnancy bleeding with cough/hemoptysis or neurologic symptoms → metastatic trophoblastic malignancy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abnormal fertilization produces proliferative hydropic villi; high hCG stimulates thyroid and ovarian receptors
Choriocarcinoma lacks chorionic villi and spreads hematogenously, especially to lungs, vagina, brain

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Quantitative **β-hCG + pelvic ultrasound**; snowstorm/multicystic placental appearance may be absent early
Evacuated tissue histopathology confirms; p57 absent in complete mole, retained in partial mole
★ Postevacuation **hCG plateau over 3 weeks or rise over 2 weeks** → evaluate GTN
Suspected neoplasia → chest imaging and stage/risk assessment; avoid biopsy of vascular vaginal metastasis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Stabilize bleeding → **suction curettage**; send tissue; give anti-D if Rh-negative
Hysterectomy an option when fertility not desired; surveillance remains necessary
Low-risk GTN → methotrexate or actinomycin D; high-risk → multiagent chemotherapy
hCG every 1–2 weeks until normal; partial: reconfirm after 1 month; complete: monthly for 6 months

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhage, thyroid storm, early hypertensive disease, invasive mole, metastatic malignancy
Chemotherapy toxicity; prognosis often excellent even with metastatic disease when treated

rows.label: Prevention
items: Reliable contraception during hCG surveillance; combined OCPs acceptable; defer pregnancy until follow-up complete
Future pregnancy → early ultrasound and postpregnancy hCG assessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Multiple gestation: high hCG with recognizable normally developing fetuses
Missed abortion: nonviable gestation without trophoblastic overgrowth

table.title: Molar subtypes
rows: Usually triploid; maternal + two paternal sets

gestational-trophoblastic-disease.evidence: Surveillance checked 2026-10-30: [FIGO 2025 update](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12411817/); remaining pathology established teaching.

hiv-infection.name: HIV infection
hiv-infection.scope: Acute HIV, testing, ART start, opportunistic infection prophylaxis, PrEP/PEP, opportunistic infections (CMV retinitis, toxoplasmosis, PJP)
hiv-infection.core: HIV progressively depletes CD4 cells; early diagnosis and suppressive ART prevent immune failure and sexual transmission.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual exposure, shared injection equipment, perinatal transmission; other STIs increase acquisition risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Acute infection 2–4 weeks post-exposure: fever, rash, sore throat, **mucosal ulcers**, diarrhea, generalized lymphadenopathy
Weight loss, thrush, recurrent candida/herpes, **extensive adult molluscum** → test HIV; dysphagia → candidal esophagitis
Child/teen: chronic fever/diarrhea, poor growth, generalized nodes, splenomegaly, **polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retroviral integration creates lifelong reservoirs; ongoing replication drives immune depletion and inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Fourth-generation Ag/Ab → HIV-1/2 differentiation assay**; discordance → HIV RNA
★ Recent exposure/acute syndrome despite negative screen → **HIV RNA**, before antibodies appear
Baseline viral load, CD4, genotype, renal/liver function, HBV/HCV/TB, pregnancy testing, **cervical cytology**
AIDS: CD4 <200 or AIDS-defining illness regardless of count
Prenatal: opt-out screening; refusal → counsel, re-offer later; never test without consent

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Start **integrase-based ART promptly**, usually bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine; assess HBV coinfection and interactions
Do not delay routine ART for genotype; cryptococcal/TB meningitis require disease-specific deferred timing
PJP: TMP-SMX; add glucocorticoid if PaO₂ <70 or A–a gradient ≥35
Toxoplasmosis: **pyrimethamine/sulfadiazine/leucovorin**, else TMP-SMX; CMV retinitis: valganciclovir, ophthalmology
Untreated/viremic mother's newborn → **triple ART** ASAP, ideally within 6 h, ≤6 weeks; suppressed mother → zidovudine alone

rows.label: Complications
items: Opportunistic infections, malignancies, wasting, neurocognitive disease, kidney disease
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome after ART; drug toxicity/interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ PJP prophylaxis: **TMP-SMX** with CD4 <200 before/starting ART; on ART, <100 or 100–200 with viremia
Toxoplasma IgG positive + CD4 <100 → prophylaxis; MAC <50 only without immediate effective ART
★ Exposure ≤72 hours → **28-day PEP: dolutegravir + TDF/emtricitabine**; do not delay for laboratory results
PrEP: TDF/emtricitabine, cabotegravir, or lenacapavir; exclude HIV first, continue serial testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: EBV mononucleosis: atypical lymphocytes, heterophile positivity; acute HIV can be heterophile-negative
Primary CNS lymphoma: often solitary lesion; biopsy after failed empiric anti-Toxoplasma treatment, earlier if serology/imaging/CSF PCR disagree
SCID/CVID: low immunoglobulins; SCID lymphopenia, no nodes; perinatal HIV: PJP, thrush, nodes, normal lymphocytes

table.title: Advanced-disease syndromes
rows: Dry cough, hypoxemia, ground-glass; sputum/BAL silver stain
Ring-enhancing mass lesions, edema/mass effect; positive IgG
Cognitive decline; non-enhancing subcortical demyelination, no mass effect

hyponatremia.name: Hyponatremia
hyponatremia.scope: Hypovolemic, euvolemic (SIADH, primary polydipsia), hypervolemic, acute vs chronic, hypertonic saline indications
hyponatremia.core: Low serum sodium reflects excess water relative to sodium; symptoms and duration determine urgency before the cause determines maintenance treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Thiazides, SSRIs, carbamazepine/oxcarbazepine, oxytocin; **hypotonic IV D5W**, postoperative state, exercise + excess water
Pulmonary/CNS disease; **small cell lung cancer** (ectopic ADH); heart failure, cirrhosis, renal failure

rows.label: Clues
items: Nausea, headache, gait instability; seizures, coma or marked confusion indicate severe cerebral edema
Orthostasis/dry mucosa suggest depletion; edema/ascites suggest excess extracellular fluid
SIADH: clinically euvolemic with inappropriately concentrated urine despite hypo-osmolality
Massive water intake, often psychiatric illness; urine osmolality below serum still favors polydipsia, even if >100

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hypotonic extracellular fluid drives water into brain; chronic adaptation makes rapid correction dangerous
ADH-mediated water retention or intake exceeding renal dilution capacity lowers sodium concentration
Low effective volume (heart failure, cirrhosis, diarrhea) → baroreceptor ADH release; total-body sodium high in edema

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Serum osmolality first: **<275 mOsm/kg** confirms hypotonicity; assess glucose and volume status
Hyperglycemia → translocational hyponatremia; severe hyperlipidemia/proteinemia → pseudohyponatremia
★ Urine osmolality **<100** → polydipsia/low solute; ≥100 → persistent ADH activity
Urine Na <20–30 suggests low effective arterial volume; >30 suggests renal loss or SIADH
Exclude adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism and renal failure before diagnosing SIADH; diuretics confound urine Na

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe neurologic symptoms → **3% saline bolus**, repeated for initial Na rise 4–6 mEq/L
Hypovolemia → isotonic saline; SIADH → fluid restriction, increased solute, remove trigger
Edematous states → fluid/sodium restriction and loop diuretic; treat heart/liver/kidney disorder
★ Chronic/unknown duration: generally limit rise to **≤8 mEq/L per 24 h**; monitor frequently
Overcorrection → desmopressin plus D5W; avoid routine vaptans in acute symptomatic cases

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute severe hyponatremia → herniation, respiratory arrest
Osmotic demyelination after rapid correction; greatest risk with alcoholism, malnutrition, hypokalemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid hypotonic maintenance fluids during high ADH states; review causative drugs
Monitor for brisk aquaresis after restoring volume or stopping thiazides

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cerebral salt wasting: neurosurgical patient, hypovolemic, high urine Na; SIADH euvolemic
Hyperosmolar hyperglycemia: measured osmolality elevated
Primary psychiatric disease: neurologic change without sodium abnormality

hyponatremia.evidence: Not checked online; established hyponatremia consensus principles.

infertility.name: Infertility
infertility.scope: Definition (failure to conceive after 12 months), initial evaluation, semen analysis (male factor), ovulatory status (midluteal progesterone), tubal and uterine factors (hysterosalpingography), ovarian reserve testing
infertility.core: No conception after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse; evaluate after 6 months at age ≥35, immediately over 40 or with risks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, PCOS, endometriosis, PID, pelvic surgery, chemotherapy, testicular injury, exogenous testosterone
Smoking, marked weight extremes, premature ovarian insufficiency, untreated endocrine disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Irregular/absent cycles → ovulatory dysfunction; galactorrhea → hyperprolactinemia; hot flashes → ovarian insufficiency
Prior ectopic pregnancy or chlamydia → tubal damage; normal cycles do not exclude male factor

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Failure of sperm production/delivery, oocyte release, fertilization, transport, or implantation; mixed factors common
Estrogen → proliferative endometrium; LH surge → ovulation
Corpus luteum **progesterone** → secretory endometrium, ↑basal body temperature

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Evaluate **both partners simultaneously**; reproductive history, sexual timing, examinations; semen analysis early
Abnormal semen result → repeat and male reproductive evaluation; do not begin with female laparoscopy
★ Ovulation uncertain → **progesterone about 7 days before expected menses**; >3 ng/mL supports ovulation
Regular 21–35-day cycles usually imply ovulation; targeted TSH, prolactin only for relevant symptoms
★ Ovulatory + normal semen → **HSG** (tubes) before laparoscopy; saline sonography: cavity; avoid in pregnancy/infection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Anovulation/PCOS → **letrozole**, clomiphene alternative; hyperprolactinemia → cabergoline; correct thyroid disease
Tubal occlusion/severe male factor → IVF, sometimes intracytoplasmic sperm injection
Unexplained infertility → ovarian stimulation with intrauterine insemination, then IVF if unsuccessful
Intercourse every 1–2 days during fertile window; avoid testosterone for fertility-seeking men

rows.label: Complications
items: Psychological distress; stimulation → ovarian hyperstimulation, multiple gestation; assisted reproduction → ectopic pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: STI prevention, tobacco cessation, weight optimization; fertility preservation before gonadotoxic treatment
Preconception folic acid and medication review

rows.label: Mimics
items: Infrequent intercourse: inadequate exposure despite normal reproductive testing
Recurrent pregnancy loss: conception occurs, followed by repeated losses

table.title: Ovarian reserve: treatment response, not natural fertility
rows: Low values suggest reduced follicular pool

infertility.evidence: Evaluation checked 2026-10-30: [ASRM 2021](https://www.asrm.org/practice-guidance/practice-committee-documents/fertility-evaluation-of-infertile-women-a-committee-opinion-2021/); treatment established reproductive guidance.

informed-consent-and-capacity.name: Informed consent and capacity
informed-consent-and-capacity.scope: Decision-making capacity, informed consent, emergency exception (implied consent), refusal of treatment, AMA discharge
informed-consent-and-capacity.core: A capable adult may accept or refuse treatment after understanding its benefits, material risks, alternatives, and consequences of refusal.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ Capacity: **understand, appreciate (own case), reason, communicate**; decision-specific, fluctuating
Competence: legal; diagnosis, age, alcohol use, incarceration, disagreement alone ≠ incapacity

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Explain benefits, material risks, alternatives/no treatment; **qualified interpreter and teach-back**
Correct delirium, intoxication, pain, communication barriers; reassess capacity
AMA request: assess capacity, explore barriers, offer safer plan, document discussion and follow-up

rows.label: Don't
items: Capable refusal → respect choice, even if life-saving or pregnant; avoid coercion, abandonment
No valid consent → possible **battery**; signed form alone insufficient
Refusing one therapy (blood) ≠ refusing all; provide other indicated care, including surgery

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Emergency + incapacity + no surrogate/directive/verified refusal → implied consent to treat
★ Parents refuse minor's life-saving transfusion → **treat emergency**; seek court authority if feasible
Incapacity without emergency → authorized surrogate; involve patient to remaining ability

rows.label: Traps
items: Psychiatric illness does not automatically remove capacity; assess the specific decision
Suicide danger may justify protective detention despite expressed desire to leave
New material procedure or changed risk → renewed consent; consent revocable anytime before procedure

table.title: Who decides
rows: Ask whom to involve; facilitate promptly; no override
Minor decides; no parental consent (state law varies)
Parents seek unproven remedy for child
Continue proven therapy; investigate remedy; CPS not first
Close; discuss after waking; no next-of-kin consent
Autonomy ≠ entitlement; physician refuses, explains, offers alternatives

informed-consent-and-capacity.evidence: Not checked online; established consent/capacity ethics; emergency and minor-consent law varies by jurisdiction.

inherited-thrombophilias.name: Inherited thrombophilias
inherited-thrombophilias.scope: Factor V Leiden (activated protein C resistance), prothrombin G20210A mutation, protein C and protein S deficiency, antithrombin III deficiency, venous thromboembolism, pregnancy complications, anticoagulation management
inherited-thrombophilias.core: Inherited procoagulant states predispose chiefly to venous thrombosis; testing matters only when results change prevention or treatment decisions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: First-degree relative with high-risk thrombophilia, young/recurrent VTE, unusual venous site
Pregnancy, estrogen, surgery, immobilization amplify risk; homozygous/combined defects are higher risk

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT, pulmonary embolism; family clustering supports inherited predisposition but may be absent
★ **Heparin resistance** suggests antithrombin deficiency; neonatal purpura fulminans suggests severe protein C deficiency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Excess clotting activity or deficient natural anticoagulants shifts hemostasis toward thrombin generation
Older exams may expect **maternal uteroplacental artery thrombosis** → placental infarction/fetal loss, not cord clot

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm suspected VTE with **compression ultrasound** or pulmonary imaging before etiologic testing
Prior/pregnancy VTE + strong family history → **Factor V Leiden**/prothrombin DNA testing; PT/aPTT normal, cannot screen
Pregnancy/estrogen lowers protein S; warfarin lowers C/S; heparin and acute clotting alter antithrombin
DNA assays reliable during acute clots; defer functional assays until confounders resolve; don't stop needed anticoagulation
No routine panel for isolated miscarriage, preeclampsia, FGR, or asymptomatic general population; MTHFR testing unhelpful

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute pregnancy VTE → **therapeutic LMWH**; UFH when rapid reversibility needed
Nonpregnant VTE → DOAC or warfarin; duration depends on provocation, recurrence, bleeding risk
Pregnancy prophylaxis depends on prior VTE and specific/family risk; low-risk heterozygosity alone often needs surveillance
★ Prior unprovoked/estrogen-related VTE generally warrants antepartum prophylaxis; prior VTE → postpartum prophylaxis
Protein C/S deficiency: overlap heparin when starting warfarin; avoid unopposed loading

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent embolism, post-thrombotic syndrome; anticoagulants → bleeding, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
Inherited thrombophilia does not establish causation for pregnancy loss; empiric heparin does not improve unexplained loss

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Avoid **estrogen-containing contraception** in high-risk thrombophilia/VTE; prophylaxis during major transient risks

rows.label: Mimics
items: APS: acquired antibodies, arterial events and characteristic obstetric morbidity
Cancer-associated thrombosis: acquired hypercoagulability with systemic/malignancy findings

inherited-thrombophilias.evidence: Pregnancy prophylaxis checked 2026-10-30: [ASH teaching guidance](https://www.hematology.org/-/media/hematology/files/clinicians/guidelines/vte/ash-teaching-slide-setvtepregnancypdffinal71923.pdf); remaining content established hematology.

intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.name: Intrapartum fetal monitoring
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.scope: Baseline fetal heart rate, variability, early decelerations, late decelerations, variable decelerations, category I II III tracings, intrauterine resuscitation
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.core: Fetal oxygenation assessment from baseline, variability, and decelerations; persistent category III requires expedited delivery after immediate resuscitation.

rows.label: Definition
items: ★ Normal baseline **110–160/min**; moderate variability **6–25 beats/min**
Bradycardia <110; tachycardia >160; baseline change lasts ≥10 minutes
Tachysystole: >5 contractions/10 minutes over 30 minutes; oxytocin excess → late decelerations

rows.label: Interpret
items: Early: mirrors contraction → head compression; benign
Late: nadir after contraction peak → uteroplacental insufficiency
Variable: abrupt fall → cord compression; prolonged: 2–10 minutes

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Category II: lateral positioning, stop oxytocin, IV fluids; correct hypotension
Persistent tachysystole with concerning tracing → **terbutaline**; recurrent variables → amnioinfusion
★ Bradycardia: exam for cord prolapse; post-epidural → **maternal hypotension**; prepare delivery

rows.label: Compare
items: **Maternal fever** commonest tachycardia, variability kept; hypoxia → low variability, late decelerations
Transient minimal variability, no decelerations → **fetal sleep**, usually <40 minutes
Late decelerations → hypoxemia → **metabolic acidosis**; acute cord compression → respiratory acidosis

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Oxygen only for **maternal hypoxemia**; older routine-oxygen answers conflict with current guidance
Moderate variability or accelerations strongly argues against current metabolic acidemia
Category II alone does not mandate cesarean; reassess response and labor progress

table.title: Three-tier interpretation
rows: Reassuring rate/variability; no late or variable decelerations
Absent variability + recurrent late/variable decelerations or bradycardia
Resuscitate; unresolved → cesarean unless fully dilated
Evaluate severe anemia; expedite if persistent

intrauterine-fetal-demise.name: Intrauterine fetal demise
intrauterine-fetal-demise.scope: Ultrasound diagnosis (absent cardiac activity), delivery methods (induction of labor, dilation and evacuation), maternal complication (DIC from retained fetus), postmortem evaluation (autopsy, karyotype)
intrauterine-fetal-demise.core: Suspected fetal death from absent movement or heart tones requires ultrasound confirmation before delivery planning and etiologic evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Placental insufficiency/FGR, hypertension, diabetes, abruption, infection, congenital anomalies, alloimmunization
Prior stillbirth, smoking, obesity, advanced maternal age, post-term pregnancy; many cases remain unexplained

rows.label: Clues
items: Reduced/absent fetal movement; absent Doppler tones alone insufficient
Bleeding or pain suggests abruption; fever suggests infection; maternal symptoms may be absent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fetal hypoxia, hemorrhage, infection, or lethal anomaly terminates circulation
Prolonged retention can release tissue factor, producing consumptive coagulopathy; uncommon with timely management

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Ultrasound: absent fetal cardiac activity**; ensure diagnostic certainty and offer confirmation
★ Evaluate **placenta/cord histology, fetal autopsy, and genetic testing**; microarray often preferred to karyotype
Obtain fetal/placental tissue or amniotic fluid for genetics; maternal blood tests cannot substitute
Maternal CBC, coagulation/fibrinogen if retention/bleeding; prompt fetomaternal hemorrhage testing before delivery
Target APS testing, syphilis and diabetes evaluation to context; routine inherited thrombophilia/TORCH panels low value

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Offer compassionate **induction or D&E**, guided by gestation, preference, expertise, and uterine scar
Second trimester: mifepristone then misoprostol; later gestation: cervical ripening/oxytocin with scar-specific precautions
★ **Cesarean rarely indicated solely for demise**; maternal safety determines route
Bleeding/infection/DIC → stabilize, expedite; trauma + free fluid → emergent **cesarean**; anti-D if Rh-negative unsensitized
Provide bereavement care, memory-making options, lactation counseling, and follow-up review of results

rows.label: Complications
items: DIC, infection, hemorrhage; profound grief, depression, post-traumatic stress

rows.label: Prevention
items: Optimize identified maternal disease, stop smoking; future pregnancy: growth assessment and tailored fetal surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Fetal sleep: temporarily reduced movement but cardiac activity present
Dating/technical error: ultrasound demonstrates living fetus despite absent handheld Doppler signal

macrocytic-anemia.name: Macrocytic anemia
macrocytic-anemia.scope: Folate deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency, pernicious anemia, hypersegmented neutrophils, methylmalonic acid and homocysteine
macrocytic-anemia.core: MCV >100 fL prompts separation of megaloblastic DNA-synthesis failure from alcohol, liver disease, hypothyroidism, reticulocytosis, and marrow disorders.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Vegan diet without supplementation, gastric bypass, ileal disease/resection, metformin, long-term **PPI** → B12 depletion
Alcohol misuse, poor intake, pregnancy, methotrexate, trimethoprim → folate depletion; stores last months, B12 years
Autoimmune gastritis → pernicious anemia; nitrous oxide functionally inactivates cobalamin

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, glossitis; ineffective erythropoiesis may raise LDH/indirect bilirubin and lower other cell lines
★ **Paresthesias, gait ataxia, impaired vibration/proprioception** → B12 deficiency, even without anemia
Smooth macro-ovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils indicate megaloblastic change

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Defective thymidine synthesis delays nuclear maturation relative to cytoplasm
B12-dependent myelin metabolism explains spinal cord/peripheral nerve injury; folate deficiency lacks this syndrome
B12 malabsorption corrected by oral intrinsic factor → **gastric IF loss** (atrophic gastritis), not ileal disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC, smear, reticulocytes, B12**; assess folate, liver tests, TSH, exposures
Borderline B12 → methylmalonic acid; renal impairment can elevate it independently
★ Suspected pernicious anemia → **anti-intrinsic-factor antibodies**; highly specific but not fully sensitive
High reticulocytes → bleeding/hemolysis; unexplained cytopenias/dysplasia → bone marrow evaluation for MDS
Coexisting iron deficiency may normalize MCV; neurologic suspicion still requires B12 evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Replace B12 before or with folate**; folate alone can conceal ongoing neurologic injury
Neurologic/severe deficiency or malabsorption → parenteral B12 initially; irreversible cause requires lifelong replacement
Dietary B12 deficiency may respond to high-dose oral replacement; folate deficiency → oral folic acid
Remove causative drug/exposure where possible; monitor reticulocyte response and count recovery

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated B12 deficiency → irreversible neurologic disability; severe disease → pancytopenia
Pernicious anemia → increased gastric adenocarcinoma and neuroendocrine tumor risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Reliable B12 supplementation for vegans**; lifelong monitoring/replacement after relevant GI surgery
Folic acid before conception and early pregnancy; improve nutrition and reduce harmful alcohol intake

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alcohol-associated macrocytosis: round macrocytes, no required megaloblastic change
Myelodysplasia: persistent multilineage cytopenia, dysplastic marrow
Reticulocytosis: polychromasia after blood loss or hemolysis

macrocytic-anemia.evidence: Not checked online; established hematology and nutritional teaching.

multiple-gestation.name: Multiple gestation
multiple-gestation.scope: Dichorionic diamniotic (lambda sign), monochorionic diamniotic (T-sign), monochorionic monoamniotic, twin-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS), selective FGR, delivery timing recommendations
multiple-gestation.core: Chorionicity and amnionicity determine twin-specific surveillance, complications, and delivery timing; establish both on first-trimester ultrasound.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dizygotic twins: ovulation induction/assisted reproduction, maternal age, family history
Monozygotic splitting timing determines placental and sac sharing

rows.label: Clues
items: Uterus larger than dates, exaggerated pregnancy symptoms; ultrasound confirms fetal number
★ Shared placenta with **oligohydramnios/polyhydramnios sequence** → TTTS; small/absent donor bladder
Selective FGR: one small twin, discordant estimated weights; assess each umbilical artery Doppler

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental vascular anastomoses permit imbalanced flow in monochorionic twins
Donor hypovolemia reduces urine; recipient hypervolemia increases urine and cardiac strain

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **First-trimester ultrasound** identifies shared placenta and intertwin membrane
Monochorionic diamniotic → ultrasound **every 2 weeks from 16 weeks** for fluid/bladders
Serial growth in all twins; Doppler and more frequent assessment when growth discordance develops
TTTS donor deepest pocket ≤2 cm, recipient ≥8 cm; staging incorporates bladder, Doppler, hydrops

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ TTTS stages II–IV at 16–26 weeks → **fetoscopic laser ablation** of placental anastomoses
Asymptomatic stage I → at least weekly surveillance; refer fetal intervention center if progression/symptoms
★ Diamniotic twins with **first twin cephalic** may deliver vaginally with experienced team
Monoamniotic twins → cesarean; fetal deterioration, preeclampsia, or severe growth issues may require earlier delivery

rows.label: Complications
items: Preterm birth, preeclampsia, anemia, gestational diabetes, postpartum hemorrhage
Monoamniotic cord entanglement; monochorionic co-twin death can cause surviving twin neurologic injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Low-dose aspirin for preeclampsia prevention; optimize iron/nutrition; single-embryo transfer reduces iatrogenic multiples

rows.label: Mimics
items: Incorrect dates/macrosomia: enlarged uterus but singleton on imaging
Twin anemia-polycythemia sequence: discordant MCA velocities without major fluid imbalance

osteoporosis.name: Osteoporosis
osteoporosis.scope: DEXA scan T-score criteria, screening guidelines, glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis, vertebral compression fractures, bisphosphonates
osteoporosis.core: Fragility fracture or markedly reduced bone density identifies skeletal weakness, often silent until hip or vertebral fracture.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Postmenopause, older age, White/Asian ancestry, BMI <20, parental fragility hip fracture, smoking, alcohol >2 drinks/day
Glucocorticoids, early or surgical menopause, hypogonadism, malabsorption, hyperthyroidism, immobility, rheumatoid arthritis

rows.label: Clues
items: Height loss, kyphosis, acute back pain with **midline point tenderness** after trivial strain suggest vertebral compression
Neurologic deficits, fever, or nocturnal pain suggest alternative spinal pathology

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bone resorption exceeds formation; microarchitecture deteriorates despite normally mineralized remaining bone
Estrogen deficiency increases osteoclast activity; steroids suppress osteoblasts and reduce calcium balance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Hip/spine DXA**; use T-scores in postmenopausal women and men ≥50
★ Hip/vertebral low-trauma fracture establishes diagnosis regardless of DXA; acute vertebral pain → **spine x-ray** before DXA
CBC, calcium, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, 25-OH vitamin D; targeted secondary-cause testing
Younger adults: Z-score ≤−2 suggests below-age bone density; T-score alone insufficient

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Alendronate or zoledronic acid** for qualifying fracture, osteoporosis-range DXA, or high FRAX risk; raloxifene/estrogen contraindicated after VTE
Osteopenia: treat if 10-year hip risk ≥3% or major osteoporotic risk ≥20%
Oral bisphosphonate: fasting water, remain upright; avoid esophageal disease, hypocalcemia, severe kidney dysfunction
Very high risk → teriparatide/romosozumab then antiresorptive; stopping denosumab requires follow-on antiresorptive
Vertebral pain: analgesia, mobilization, short bracing; procedures reserved for selected refractory cases

rows.label: Complications
items: ★ **Hip fracture** → immobility, thromboembolism, excess mortality
Bisphosphonates: rare jaw osteonecrosis/atypical femur fracture; denosumab: hypocalcemia, rebound vertebral fractures

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Screen **women ≥65**, younger postmenopausal women at increased risk; evidence insufficient for routine male screening
**Smoking cessation**, less heavy alcohol outrank supplements; weight-bearing/resistance exercise, fall prevention, dietary calcium/vitamin D
Prednisone-equivalent ≥2.5 mg/day for >3 months → fracture-risk assessment; prevent with **alendronate**, not estrogen/raloxifene

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomalacia: defective mineralization, low phosphate, elevated alkaline phosphatase
Myeloma: anemia, renal injury, lytic lesions; metastatic fracture: destructive focal lesion

osteoporosis.evidence: Screening checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF 2025](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/osteoporosis-screening%20); treatment: established fracture-risk framework.

ovarian-cancer.name: Ovarian cancer
ovarian-cancer.scope: Epithelial ovarian carcinoma, CA-125, pelvic ultrasound, peritoneal carcinomatosis, germ cell tumors, sex cord-stromal tumors, surgical staging and cytoreduction, platinum-based chemotherapy
ovarian-cancer.core: Persistent bloating, early satiety, pelvic symptoms, or an adnexal mass—especially after menopause—requires evaluation for an often late-presenting malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, nulliparity, BRCA1/2 or Lynch syndrome; family history of breast/ovarian cancer
Endometriosis associated with clear-cell/endometrioid subtypes; pregnancy and combined contraceptives reduce epithelial risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Older patient + ascites, large/fixed pelvic mass, weight loss, pleural effusion, obstruction → **epithelial** carcinoma
Young patient with rapidly enlarging mass → germ cell tumor; estrogen/androgen effects → stromal tumor
Postmenopausal bleeding with adnexal mass → consider estrogen-secreting granulosa tumor and endometrial disease
★ **Palpable ovary after menopause** → abnormal (ovaries atrophy); pelvic ultrasound

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Many high-grade serous tumors arise in distal fallopian tube epithelium
Transcoelomic seeding produces peritoneal/omental disease; hormone secretion depends on tumor lineage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Transvaginal ultrasound** first; solid components, papillary projections, vascularity, ascites increase suspicion
★ **CA-125** supports risk assessment/monitoring, not diagnosis or average-risk screening
Young/complex mass → β-hCG, AFP, LDH; suspected stromal tumor → inhibin/sex hormones
Suspected malignancy → CT abdomen/pelvis/chest and gynecologic oncology; definitive histology and staging usually surgical
Isolated resectable mass → avoid aspiration; advanced disease → biopsy before neoadjuvant chemotherapy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Epithelial carcinoma → **surgical staging/cytoreduction + carboplatin/paclitaxel** according to stage
Poor upfront surgical candidate → tissue confirmation, neoadjuvant platinum chemotherapy, interval cytoreduction
Germ cell malignancy → fertility-sparing surgery when feasible; stage IA dysgerminoma may avoid chemotherapy
Higher-risk germ cell tumors → bleomycin/etoposide/cisplatin
Selected BRCA/HRD-associated disease → PARP-inhibitor maintenance after platinum response

rows.label: Complications
items: Peritoneal carcinomatosis, ascites, malignant obstruction, VTE; chemotherapy neuropathy/myelosuppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **No routine CA-125/ultrasound screening** in asymptomatic average-risk patients
Genetic counseling/testing; hereditary high-risk patients → discuss risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy after childbearing

rows.label: Mimics
items: Endometrioma: cyclic pain, ground-glass ultrasound; CA-125 can rise
Meigs syndrome: benign ovarian fibroma plus ascites/pleural effusion; no peritoneal implants

table.title: Tumor markers
rows: Often bilateral; psammoma bodies; WT1+, p53 abnormal

ovarian-cysts.name: Ovarian cysts
ovarian-cysts.scope: Follicular cyst, corpus luteum cyst, theca lutein cyst (hyperstimulation), mature cystic teratoma (dermoid), unilocular vs multilocular, surveillance intervals, cystectomy indications, cyst rupture
ovarian-cysts.core: Most reproductive-age ovarian cysts are benign; morphology, symptoms, menopausal status, and persistence determine observation versus surgery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Ovulatory cycles, early pregnancy; ovulation induction → **hyperstimulated ovaries**; very high hCG → bilateral enlargement
Postmenopausal adnexal masses carry higher malignancy risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Incidental mass, pelvic pressure, unilateral discomfort; sudden pain after intercourse/exertion suggests rupture
★ Sudden severe pain with vomiting → **torsion**; syncope/hypotension → major intraperitoneal bleeding

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Functional lesions arise during ovulation; dermoids contain differentiated germ-cell tissues

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Pregnancy test first; **transvaginal ultrasound** characterizes wall, septations, solid elements, flow, free fluid
Simple unilocular: thin wall, anechoic, no solid vascular component; multiloculation warrants closer characterization
Papillary/solid vascular components, thick septa, ascites → malignancy evaluation; CA-125 nonspecific premenopausally
Normal Doppler flow does not exclude torsion; urgent clinical concern overrides reassuring imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Stable functional/hemorrhagic cyst → analgesia, recheck after menses; unresolved → repeat ultrasound in **6–12 weeks**
Asymptomatic simple cyst above 5–7 cm premenopause, 3–5 cm postmenopause → ultrasound around 6–12 months
★ Hemodynamic instability → IV fluids/blood and urgent laparoscopy; torsion → detorsion with ovarian preservation
Persistent/enlarging, symptomatic, large, suspicious mass → surgery/referral
OCPs do not hasten functional-cyst resolution; older exam questions may expect OCP + 6-week recheck

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemoperitoneum, ovarian infarction, reduced ovarian reserve after surgery

rows.label: Prevention
items: Ovulation suppression may reduce new functional cyst formation; counsel urgent reassessment for acute pain

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG with pregnancy outside uterus
Tubo-ovarian abscess: fever, cervical motion tenderness, inflammatory complex mass

table.title: Cyst identities
rows: Luteal/early pregnancy; tender mass, crenulated vascular wall, hemorrhage
Bilateral multicystic ovaries; regress as hCG falls
Young; complex echogenic mass; fat, teeth, calcification

ovarian-cysts.evidence: Simple-cyst thresholds checked 2026-10-30: [SRU 2019 consensus](https://pubs.rsna.org/doi/10.1148/radiol.2019191354); acute management established teaching.

pelvic-organ-prolapse.name: Pelvic organ prolapse
pelvic-organ-prolapse.scope: Anterior compartment (cystocele), posterior compartment (rectocele, enterocele), apical compartment (uterine prolapse, vaginal vault prolapse, procidentia), pelvic floor muscle training, pessary, surgical repair
pelvic-organ-prolapse.core: Loss of pelvic support causes a vaginal bulge with pressure, urinary symptoms, or obstructed defecation, often worse when standing or straining.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Vaginal births, increasing age, menopause, obesity, connective-tissue weakness
Chronic cough/constipation, heavy lifting; hysterectomy predisposes to vaginal vault descent

rows.label: Clues
items: Visible/palpable protrusion, incomplete bladder emptying, stress leakage, need to splint vagina for defecation
★ **Urinary retention or hydronephrosis** with advanced descent → evaluate obstruction promptly
Symptoms improve supine; mucosal rubbing can produce spotting or ulceration

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Levator ani injury and fascial/ligamentous failure permit descent of one or several vaginal compartments

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pelvic examination during Valsalva**, sometimes standing; isolate compartments with speculum
POP-Q stages descent relative to hymen; measure postvoid residual when voiding symptoms present
Urinalysis for urinary symptoms; creatinine/renal ultrasound when severe obstruction suspected
Reduce prolapse during cough stress testing to unmask occult stress incontinence before surgery

rows.label: Tx
items: Asymptomatic prolapse → observation; bothersome mild disease → pelvic floor muscle training
★ **Vaginal pessary** for conservative treatment, frail/high surgical risk; fit, teach removal, schedule mucosal checks
Vaginal estrogen for atrophic mucosa when suitable; does not restore structural support
★ Persistent symptoms → compartment repair plus **apical suspension** when support deficient
No future vaginal intercourse desired → colpocleisis; preservation/reconstruction chosen according to goals

rows.label: Complications
items: Ulceration, recurrent UTI, retention, obstructive kidney injury; recurrence after repair
Neglected pessary → erosion/fistula; surgery → dyspareunia, new urinary leakage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Weight reduction, treat constipation/cough, reduce straining; pelvic floor exercises and pessary follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: Urethral diverticulum: focal anterior mass, postvoid dribbling, recurrent infection
Vaginal cyst: discrete lesion without generalized descent during strain

table.title: Compartments
rows: Small bowel → upper posterior vagina/vault; peristalsis
Entire uterus prolapses beyond vaginal introitus

pelvic-organ-prolapse.evidence: Not checked online; established urogynecology evaluation and conservative/surgical management.

postpartum-care.name: Postpartum care
postpartum-care.scope: Normal puerperal changes, lochia, uterine involution, perineal and cesarean wound healing, breastfeeding, postpartum depression screening, routine postpartum visit
postpartum-care.core: Postpartum care is an ongoing assessment of recovery, mood, infant feeding, contraception, and chronic disease after every birth.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ All postpartum patients; assess support, sleep, safety, sexual health, and reproductive goals

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Contact within **3 weeks**; comprehensive visit by **12 weeks**, with earlier risk-based review
Hypertensive disorder → BP within 7–10 days; severe hypertension → within 72 hours

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Edinburgh or PHQ-9 depression screen; assess suicidality directly after positive self-harm response
BP, bleeding, fundal tenderness; inspect perineum/incision for erythema, drainage, separation
Observe latch/milk transfer; frequent feeds, lactation support; cracked nipples → correct positioning

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Heavy bleeding (pad soaked <1 hour), fever, dyspnea, severe headache → urgent evaluation
Mood screen positive → diagnostic interview, psychotherapy/SSRI; psychosis → emergency hospitalization
Increasing wound pain/purulence → evaluate infection; breast fluctuance → ultrasound for abscess

rows.label: Traps
items: Ovulation may precede first period; discuss contraception before discharge
Lactational contraception: amenorrhea, exclusive frequent breastfeeding, infant <6 months
Postpartum hypertension and cardiomyopathy can first appear after discharge

table.title: Expected recovery
rows: Red rubra → pink serosa → white/yellow alba
Descends daily; near prepregnancy size by 6 weeks
Pain improves; pulling normal if intact; keep clean
Early cramping and fluid loss; breastfeeding intensifies cramping

postpartum-care.evidence: Visit timing checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG postpartum care](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/05/optimizing-postpartum-care); normal physiology established teaching.

postpartum-hemorrhage.name: Postpartum hemorrhage
postpartum-hemorrhage.scope: Primary postpartum hemorrhage (uterine atony, lacerations, retained placenta, coagulopathy), secondary postpartum hemorrhage (retained products of conception, endometritis), barrier methods, surgical management
postpartum-hemorrhage.core: Excessive bleeding after delivery demands simultaneous resuscitation and cause-directed control: Tone, Trauma, Tissue and Thrombin.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Uterine overdistention, prolonged/augmented labor, chorioamnionitis, magnesium, prior PPH → atony
Operative delivery → trauma; placenta accreta/retention → tissue; abruption/sepsis → coagulopathy

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Boggy enlarged uterus** → atony; firm uterus with bleeding → laceration or other cause
Jagged/incomplete placenta, vessels to membrane edge (**succenturiate lobe**) → retained tissue; oozing → coagulopathy
Shock exceeding visible loss → concealed hematoma; post-cesarean distention, hematocrit drop → **intra-abdominal hemorrhage**
Delayed bleeding >24 hours to weeks postpartum → retained products, endometritis or subinvolution

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Myometrial contraction compresses placental-bed vessels; failed contraction or disrupted tissue prevents hemostasis
Vulvar hematoma: **pudendal artery** branch, often operative delivery; vaginal/uterine arteries → deep or retroperitoneal

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Quantify blood loss; US definition **≥1000 mL or hypovolemia within 24 hours**, regardless of route
WHO 2025 earlier treatment trigger: ≥500 mL, or ≥300 mL with abnormal hemodynamic signs
Assess uterine tone, inspect birth canal/placenta; CBC, coagulation studies, fibrinogen and crossmatch
Ultrasound for suspected retained products; avoid delaying control in active unstable bleeding
Inversion: round fleshy introitus mass after cord traction, absent abdominal fundus, shock

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Hemorrhage team, two large IVs, warmed balanced blood resuscitation; massage, empty bladder, **oxytocin**
★ **Tranexamic acid within 3 hours** alongside first-response treatment
Refractory atony → **balloon/vacuum**, embolization if stable; compression sutures/arterial ligation or hysterectomy
Laceration → repair; retained tissue → evacuation; inversion → manual replacement before uterotonics
Endometritis → **clindamycin + gentamicin**

rows.label: Complications
items: DIC, AKI, shock, death; severe ischemia → Sheehan syndrome
Transfusion complications and hysterectomy-related fertility loss; delayed anemia impairs recovery

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prophylactic **oxytocin after delivery**, active third-stage management and antenatal anemia treatment
Risk assessment, blood availability and team readiness; routine prophylactic TXA not recommended for vaginal birth

rows.label: Mimics
items: Amniotic fluid embolism: sudden hypoxia/collapse with DIC
Pulmonary embolism: hypoxia/chest pain without primary uterine blood loss

postpartum-mood-disorders.name: Postpartum mood disorders
postpartum-mood-disorders.scope: Postpartum blues (onset <2 weeks, self-limited, reassurance), postpartum depression (MDD criteria, Edinburgh screening, SSRIs, psychotherapy), postpartum psychosis (delusions, infanticide risk, emergent hospitalization)
postpartum-mood-disorders.core: After birth, distinguish transient tearfulness from sustained depressive illness and from psychosis threatening maternal or infant safety.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior depression/postpartum depression, anxiety, poor support, trauma, sleep loss, pregnancy complications
★ **Bipolar disorder or previous postpartum psychosis** → especially high psychosis recurrence risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Anhedonia, guilt, impaired bonding/function, appetite/sleep changes beyond infant-care demands
★ **Suicidality, command hallucinations, infant-focused delusions**, confusion, mania → emergency
Unwanted distressing intrusive thoughts with preserved insight differ from fixed psychotic beliefs

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormonal withdrawal, circadian disruption, and psychosocial stress interact with mood-disorder vulnerability
Postpartum psychosis frequently represents a bipolar-spectrum episode rather than schizophrenia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale or PHQ-9** screens; positive result requires diagnostic interview
MDD: ≥5 symptoms including depressed mood/anhedonia, ≥2 weeks, clinically significant impairment
★ Screen for **bipolar disorder before antidepressants**; assess suicide/infant-harm intent, access, supervision
Check TSH/CBC for suggestive medical mimics; mania/psychosis → urgent psychiatric assessment

rows.label: Tx
items: Ensure safe infant care, assess support, address sleep; do not leave psychotic patient alone with infant
Depression: CBT/interpersonal psychotherapy; moderate/severe → SSRI, often sertraline during breastfeeding
Severe postpartum depression: specialist-directed zuranolone or other treatment; weigh sedation and feeding considerations
Psychosis: inpatient antipsychotic ± lithium; ECT for severe, catatonic, suicidal, or refractory illness

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, infanticide, impaired attachment/child development, recurrent depressive or bipolar episodes

rows.label: Prevention
items: Protect sleep, mobilize family support; prior severe illness → antenatal psychiatric plan and postpartum prophylaxis
Repeat mood screening through pregnancy/postpartum; establish follow-up before discharge

rows.label: Mimics
items: Postpartum thyroiditis: biochemical thyroid dysfunction with systemic features
Normal adjustment: transient stress without pervasive anhedonia or sustained impairment

table.title: Course and disposition
rows: Persistent symptoms; may occur throughout first year
Outpatient treatment if safe; escalate for severity
Emergency hospitalization; protect mother and infant

postpartum-mood-disorders.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG screening](https://www.acog.org/programs/perinatal-mental-health/patient-screening), [2026 zuranolone update](https://doi.org/10.1097/AOG.0000000000006093); other management established teaching.

preterm-labor.name: Preterm labor
preterm-labor.scope: Preterm labor (<37 weeks), cervical insufficiency, tocolysis (indomethacin, nifedipine), antenatal corticosteroids (betamethasone), magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection, GBS chemoprophylaxis
preterm-labor.core: Regular contractions with cervical change before 37 weeks; briefly delay eligible early births to improve neonatal outcomes, without prolonging unsafe pregnancies.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior spontaneous preterm birth, short cervix, multiple gestation, infection, smoking, uterine anomalies
Cervical surgery or prior painless second-trimester loss suggests cervical insufficiency

rows.label: Clues
items: Pelvic pressure, backache, increased discharge, contractions; assess membrane rupture and bleeding
Fever, uterine tenderness, fetal tachycardia → intraamniotic infection; maternal/fetal instability changes delivery timing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature inflammatory/uterine activation versus mechanically weak cervix with painless dilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Sterile speculum examination** for pooling and cervix; ultrasound dates pregnancy and assesses presentation
Transvaginal cervical length; selected symptomatic cases: negative fetal fibronectin predicts low imminent birth risk
Collect GBS culture, urine studies; exclude previa before digital examination with bleeding

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Birth within 7 days, **24–33 6/7 weeks** → betamethasone; selected untreated 34–36 6/7-week pregnancies also eligible
★ Delivery expected <32 weeks → **magnesium sulfate** for neuroprotection, not primary tocolysis
Tocolysis: 48 hours for steroids/transfer; no maintenance; late-preterm steroids avoided with pregestational diabetes
★ **No tocolysis** with infection, significant abruption, severe preeclampsia, or fetal compromise; proceed toward delivery
Intrapartum penicillin for positive/unknown GBS; no routine antibiotics for intact membranes without infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Neonatal RDS, IVH, NEC, sepsis, cerebral palsy; magnesium toxicity → hyporeflexia, respiratory depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Singleton short cervix ≤20 mm before 24 weeks → vaginal progesterone; consider at 21–25 mm
Cervical insufficiency/prior qualifying loss → cerclage; prior preterm birth + cervix <25 mm before 24 weeks
17-hydroxyprogesterone caproate withdrawn 2023; progesterone without short cervix not routinely recommended
Older exam questions may expect 17-hydroxyprogesterone from 16–20 weeks after prior spontaneous preterm birth

rows.label: Mimics
items: Braxton Hicks: no progressive dilation
Cervical insufficiency: painless dilation, minimal contractions
PPROM: membrane rupture precedes labor; distinct latency-antibiotic pathway

rh-alloimmunization.name: Rh alloimmunization
rh-alloimmunization.scope: Rh(D) and other red cell alloimmunization (Kell, Duffy), anti-D immune globulin prophylaxis, indirect Coombs titer monitoring, fetomaternal hemorrhage (Kleihauer-Betke), middle cerebral artery Doppler for fetal anemia
rh-alloimmunization.core: Maternal IgG against fetal red-cell antigens crosses the placenta, causing fetal anemia, hydrops, and neonatal hemolysis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Antigen-negative mother/positive fetus; prior pregnancy, transfusion, bleeding, trauma, invasive procedures
Anti-D, anti-Kell, and anti-Duffy clinically significant; ABO incompatibility usually milder

rows.label: Clues
items: Often asymptomatic mother; fetal ascites, skin edema, placentomegaly, cardiomegaly
Neonate: early jaundice, pallor, reticulocytosis, **positive direct Coombs**; severe disease → cardiovascular collapse

rows.label: Pathophys
items: First exposure sensitizes; subsequent antigen exposure produces an anamnestic response
Kell antibodies additionally suppress erythropoiesis; low titers can still cause severe disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First prenatal visit: ABO/Rh type + **indirect Coombs**; repeat before routine antenatal prophylaxis
Antibody → **paternal antigen typing**; negative (certain paternity) → no fetal risk; else fetal typing, titers
★ Critical titer, often **1:16**, or previously affected pregnancy → middle cerebral artery Doppler
MCA peak systolic velocity >1.5 MoM → fetal blood sampling; Kell warrants specialist surveillance
Kleihauer-Betke quantifies hemorrhage for dosing: **300 µg covers 30 mL fetal whole blood**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe preterm fetal anemia → **intrauterine transfusion**; near term → delivery
Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia → phototherapy; severe hemolysis → exchange transfusion

rows.label: Complications
items: High-output heart failure, stillbirth, bilirubin encephalopathy, delayed neonatal anemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Unsensitized Rh-negative mother: **anti-D immune globulin** at 28 weeks and within 72 hours postpartum
Sensitizing event → dose now; lasts ~12 weeks, repeat at 28; postpartum only if Rh-positive/unknown infant
★ Established anti-D sensitization → prophylaxis ineffective; no equivalent prophylaxis for Kell/Duffy
ACOG 2024: routine Rh testing/prophylaxis may be forgone for abortion/loss before 12 weeks

rows.label: Mimics
items: Parvovirus: nonimmune hydrops with negative maternal antibody screen
ABO hemolysis: may affect first pregnancy; fetal hydrops uncommon

rh-alloimmunization.evidence: Prophylaxis checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG Rh guidance](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/the-rh-factor-how-it-can-affect-your-pregnancy), [2024 update](https://doi.org/10.1097/AOG.0000000000005733); remaining content established teaching.

teratogens.name: Teratogens
teratogens.scope: Valproate and carbamazepine (neural tube defects), ACE inhibitors, isotretinoin, lithium (Ebstein anomaly), warfarin, alcohol (fetal alcohol syndrome), high-dose folic acid supplementation
teratogens.core: Exposure timing and agent determine fetal harm; review medications before conception and substitute safer treatments while preserving maternal disease control.

rows.label: Use
items: Preconception counseling, exposure assessment, and selection of pregnancy-compatible drugs
Inadvertent early oral contraceptive exposure → not teratogenic; reassure, no invasive testing
Live vaccines (MMR, varicella) contraindicated in pregnancy; give postpartum

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Weeks 3–8 postconception: organogenesis → malformations; later exposure → growth/functional injury

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ **Alcohol**: poor growth/development, smooth philtrum, thin upper lip, short palpebral fissures

rows.label: Avoid
items: ★ **Isotretinoin contraindicated**; pregnancy testing and effective contraception required
Valproate generally avoided when alternatives effective; do not abruptly stop antiseizure drugs
ACE inhibitor → labetalol/nifedipine for pregnancy hypertension; warfarin usually → LMWH

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Prior NTD pregnancy → **folic acid 4 mg/day**, preconception through first trimester
Antiseizure exposure: folate **≥0.4 mg/day**; optimal higher dose uncertain, individualize
Lithium: levels, renal/thyroid tests; early exposure → detailed fetal cardiac assessment

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ No safe alcohol threshold; exposure alone does not mandate pregnancy termination
Mechanical heart valves may require individualized warfarin decisions despite fetal risks
Folate lowers NTD risk but does not erase valproate-associated malformations or developmental harm

table.title: Agent → characteristic fetal injury
rows: Neural tube defects; valproate neurodevelopmental toxicity
Fetal renal injury, oligohydramnios, skull hypoplasia
Increased cardiac malformation risk, including Ebstein anomaly
Nasal hypoplasia, stippled epiphyses, fetal bleeding
Retinoid-like craniofacial, CNS malformations; reduce supplements

urinary-incontinence.name: Urinary incontinence
urinary-incontinence.core: Involuntary urine leakage is classified by triggers, urgency, bladder emptying, and ability to reach a toilet; reversible contributors often coexist.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childbirth, pelvic surgery, aging, obesity; diabetes, neurologic disease, prostate enlargement
Diuretics, sedatives, anticholinergics, constipation, infection, impaired mobility/cognition worsen control

rows.label: Clues
items: History: timing, volume, dysuria, weak stream, nocturia, fluid intake, obstetric/surgical and neurologic history
★ **New saddle anesthesia, leg weakness, retention** → urgent cauda equina evaluation
Continuous leakage after pelvic surgery/radiation suggests fistula; recurrent UTIs/hematuria require further investigation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stress: aging/multiparity weaken pelvic floor → **urethral hypermobility**, low sphincter tone
Urge: **uninhibited detrusor contractions** (detrusor instability), worsened by caffeine; MS lesion → low residual
Overflow: **detrusor underactivity/acontractile bladder** (MS, diabetes, stroke) or outlet obstruction → high residual
Functional impairment can prevent continence despite intact lower urinary tract function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis + voiding diary**, focused pelvic/prostate and neurologic examination; review medications
Cough stress test with reasonably full bladder; assess prolapse, atrophy, fecal impaction
**Q-tip excursion >30°** on Valsalva → urethral hypermobility (urethrocele)
★ Suspected retention/emptying symptoms → **postvoid residual**; persistent >200 mL suggests inadequate emptying
No routine initial urodynamics/cystoscopy; uncertainty, hematuria, refractory symptoms → additional testing

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat reversible contributor; mixed incontinence → target most bothersome component
★ **Pelvic floor training/bladder training** underpin conservative care; weight loss, reduce caffeine, timed voiding
Urgency drugs: mirabegron or antimuscarinic (oxybutynin); discuss cognitive risk and avoid antimuscarinics with retention
Mirabegron may increase BP; avoid severe uncontrolled hypertension; refractory urgency → botulinum toxin or neuromodulation
Genitourinary syndrome of menopause → local vaginal estrogen when suitable; not systemic estrogen for leakage

rows.label: Complications
items: Dermatitis, falls from rushing, social isolation, sleep disruption
Overflow → hydronephrosis/renal injury; bladder botulinum toxin → retention, UTI

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication review, accessible toilet, mobility aids; bowel regularity, maintain strength and weight

rows.label: Mimics
items: Polyuria: high urine volume from hyperglycemia/diuresis rather than primary storage failure
Vaginal fistula: constant leakage unrelated to voiding urge or exertion

vaginitis.name: Vaginitis
vaginitis.scope: Bacterial vaginosis, Trichomoniasis, Vulvovaginal candidiasis, atrophic vaginitis, genitourinary syndrome of menopause
vaginitis.core: Vaginal discharge or irritation requires distinction among dysbiosis, sexually transmitted protozoal infection, yeast overgrowth, and hypoestrogenic mucosal change.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: BV: new partners, douching; trichomoniasis: sexual exposure
Candida: antibiotics, pregnancy, diabetes, immunosuppression; atrophy: menopause or other hypoestrogenic states
Prepubertal: hand inoculation of respiratory pathogens during URI

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus, dysuria, dyspareunia; discharge appearance overlaps, so symptoms alone insufficient
★ **Fever, lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness** → evaluate PID rather than isolated vaginitis
Postmenopausal bleeding needs assessment beyond assuming atrophy
★ Prepubertal **foul purulent/bloody discharge** → retained vaginal **foreign body**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: BV: lactobacilli depleted, anaerobes expand; Candida causes inflammatory overgrowth
Low estrogen thins epithelium and reduces lactobacilli → mucosal fragility and elevated vaginal pH

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Vaginal pH, saline/KOH microscopy**, history and examination; NAAT improves infectious diagnosis
BV: ≥3 Amsel—discharge, ↑pH, clue cells, amine odor; Gardnerella culture unhelpful (normal flora)
★ Suspected trichomoniasis + negative wet mount → **NAAT**, not reassurance
Recurrent/complicated Candida → culture or PCR for species; asymptomatic colonization alone needs no treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **oral metronidazole 7 days in women**; treat partners, abstain until completed/resolved
BV → oral metronidazole 7 days or vaginal metronidazole/clindamycin, **no routine partner treatment**, ACOG: treat if recurrent; treat symptomatic pregnancy
Candida → topical azole/nystatin or oral fluconazole; **pregnancy: topical azole 7 days**, avoid oral fluconazole
GSM → moisturizers/lubricants, then low-dose vaginal estrogen for persistent symptoms
Recurrent BV: ACOG 2025 considers male-partner metronidazole + topical clindamycin; older boards omit

rows.label: Complications
items: BV/trichomoniasis associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and increased STI acquisition
Recurrent symptoms → reassess diagnosis, adherence, reinfection, diabetes or resistant/non-albicans yeast

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **retest women at about 3 months**; condoms
Avoid douching/irritants; no routine partner treatment for uncomplicated Candida

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervicitis: endocervical mucopus, friability, positive GC/CT NAAT
Contact dermatitis: external irritation after product exposure
Sarcoma botryoides: girl with bleeding, grape-like polypoid vaginal mass
